subject.title: [Bug]: CLI-backed agents cannot execute on connected nodes

question: Should CLI-backed agents receive a node-only projection of the existing `exec` tool, or a separate dedicated node-execution tool that maps to the same approval pipeline?
rationale: Both designs can repair the bug, but the permanent model-facing contract and prevention of duplicate Gateway-host shell access require explicit owner intent.

options.title: Node-only `exec` projection
options.body: Expose `exec` through loopback MCP only when node execution is allowed, with the host fixed or constrained to `node` and existing approvals reused.

options.title: Dedicated node execution tool
options.body: Add a separate model-facing node shell tool that reuses the existing approval and `system.run` implementation without exposing Gateway-host exec.

recommendation.title: Node-only `exec` projection
recommendation.body: Expose `exec` through loopback MCP only when node execution is allowed, with the host fixed or constrained to `node` and existing approvals reused.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the current affected implementation, recently tightened its sandbox boundary, and is assigned to the issue.
